content.comment_body: Good evening, we want to monitor our machines at work and track their power usage throughout the week, including when they are switched on and off, as well as the speeds at which they operate. I'm considering installing a [product_name] on each machine since it provides the necessary inputs and includes four analog inputs suitable for clamp meter measurements. Is it possible to use a [product_name] in every machine and send data via Ethernet to a [product_name] that would collect all information centrally? I know about [product_name], but we only have access to TIA Basic, and upgrading to Professional is quite costly. Thanks.

Yes, it is possible for a [product_name] to communicate with a [product_name]. The [product_name] can act as either the client or the server. In my view, it is simpler if the [product_name] functions as the client, while the [product_name] operates as the server.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing how to network multiple [product_name] devices, which serve as remote I/O to monitor machine data, and connect them to a central [product_name] using Ethernet. The focus is on utilizing analog inputs for measurements and making use of the more cost-effective TIA Basic software rather than pricier alternatives. The conversation confirms that this setup is technically feasible and addresses client-server configuration choices and budget constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: The user plans to link several [product_name] devices with a [product_name] using TIA Basic software and is looking to efficiently collect machine input data across the network.
